definitions.explanation: The pair of small strokes written at the upper right of a kana to mark a voiced consonant, as in が, ざ, だ, and ば.

examples.japanese: 「か」に{濁点|だくてん}をつけると「が」になる。
{子|こ}どもは{濁点|だくてん}のある{字|じ}を{読|よ}み{間違|まちが}えやすい。
examples.english: Children easily misread characters that have a dakuten.

examples.japanese: {濁点|だくてん}は{清音|せいおん}を{濁音|だくおん}に{変|か}える{記号|きごう}で、かなの{右上|みぎうえ}に{小|ちい}さく{書|か}く。
examples.english: The dakuten is a mark that turns a voiceless sound into a voiced one, written small at the upper right of a kana.

notes:
The voicing mark written at the upper right of a kana to indicate a voiced consonant: か becomes が, さ becomes ざ, た becomes だ, は becomes ば. Colloquially called {点々|てんてん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {濁点|だくてん}をつける: to add a dakuten
- {濁点|だくてん}をとる: to remove a dakuten
- {濁点|だくてん}つきの{字|じ}: a character with a dakuten

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {半濁点|はんだくてん}: handakuten — the small circle that turns は into ぱ
- {濁音|だくおん}: voiced sound — the voiced syllable itself, the result of adding a {濁点|だくてん}
